metadata.title: Sugar #11 — El Niño + Hormuz Compound Thesis
metadata.subtitle: Feb'27 SB calls: 18¢ ×2 (May 22) + 19.5¢ ×1 (Aug 12) — compound thesis

thesis.headline: Sep 3: Oct SB −3.4% to 18.07¢ (intraday low 17.65¢) a day after a 16.75-month high of 18.77¢. Trigger: India halved dealer stock-holding limits (400→200 MT, Sep 15–Nov 20), read as less need for the 1 MMT import window; record fund longs liquidated. Second failed test of ~18.7¢. Deficit stack unchanged; Mar'27 SBH7 19.04¢.
thesis.summary: The Sep 2 push to 18.77¢ (Reuters: Indian tightness, a 50 mm rain forecast for Ribeirão Preto set to halt harvest, EU/Thai output cuts, and ISO's Sep 1 flip to a −200k MT 2026/27 deficit from a +1.1 MMT 2025/26 surplus) reversed hard on Sep 3: Oct SB traded 18.67→17.65 and settled 18.07¢ (−3.4%) on the heaviest volume of the rally; Mar'27 SBH7 19.64→19.04¢, ~18.96¢ in the Sep 4 pre-open. Trigger: India's government halved the dealer stock-holding limit to 200 MT (from 400) for Sep 15–Nov 20 to force hoarded stock onto the domestic market — traders read it as India needing less of the 1 MMT nil-duty import window, and domestic Indian prices are already ~₹2,000/qtl off their highs on fortnightly quota releases. Fuel: funds were a record 70,766 net-long London whites (COT to Aug 25, most since 2011), so a bearish headline became a liquidation — same pattern as Aug 28's BRL-driven reversal from 18.66¢. Macro was supportive, not the cause: BRL firmed 5.19→5.09 and WTI ran $85→$91 over the week, which points at India + positioning rather than a fundamental break. Technically 18.66–18.77¢ is now a double top; 17.65¢ (Sep 3 low) and 17.44¢ (Aug 28 low) are the lines — a close through both turns this into a failed breakout rather than a pullback. Nothing in the deficit stack changed (ISO −200k, Green Pool −3.3 MMT, StoneX −1.7, EU −19%, monsoon 13% below normal as of Sep 2, El Niño intact). Conviction trimmed 83→80 for the crowded-long/technical risk, not the thesis. Correction to the Aug 30 note: UNICA's 2H-August 2026 report is NOT out yet (due ~Sep 10); the 38.31 MMT / +3.15% ethanol figures traced to the 2H-Aug 2025 report and have been removed. Next: COT (Sep 4, week to Sep 1) for whether longs grew into the high; UNICA 2H-Aug ~Sep 10; India's Oct 31 quota decision. Position: GTC to add 1× Feb'27 19.5¢ call raised to 1.18 (mid ~1.30) — it fills on a second flush, not a bounce.

elNino.probabilityWindow: El Niño Advisory ACTIVE (NOAA CPC, Aug 2026) — event formed and intensifying
elNino.strongEventOdds: 95% very strong (Niño 3.4/RONI ≥ +2.0°C) — up from 81% in July's CPC assessment; 69% chance RONI reaches +2.5°C+, which would exceed every El Niño on record since 1950
elNino.soiNote: NOAA's Aug RONI forecast puts the median Oct-Dec value at +2.66°C (middle 50% range +2.37 to +2.95°C); little indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027

millMix.brazilOutputNote: 2026/27 through May: sugar mix collapsed to 41.4% (from 50.1% a year ago) as mills pivot to ethanol — C-S sugar output 6.84 MMT, -2.0% YoY. This is the 'mill mix shift' leg of the tail scenario actually happening. 2H-July update: crush -8.4% YoY, sugar output -17.6% YoY, with the ethanol blend mandate raised to 32%. USDA's full-season 2026/27 Sugar Annual still projects the mix averaging closer to 48% sugar / 52% ethanol for the year — meaning the mid-year prints (41.4%, -17.6%) are running well below even that already-bearish full-season forecast. CORRECTION (Sep 4): the '2H-August UNICA report' cited on Aug 30 (38.31 MMT crush, ethanol +3.15%) was UNICA's 2H-Aug 2025 release, not 2026 — removed. UNICA's 2H-Aug 2026 report is due ~Sep 10; 1H-Aug 2026 figures also remain unconfirmed. Last hard data point is still 2H-July (41.4% mix, sugar -17.6% YoY).

catalystTimeline.event: Indian monsoon — LIVE: cumulative deficit 13% below normal as of Sep 2 (IMD), unchanged from Aug 26 and down from 42% on Jun 30; Earth Science Ministry warns of the weakest monsoon in 11 years; IMD expects below-normal September rain

India CONFIRMED: 1 MMT nil-duty raw import quota (first in ~10 yrs) + bulk stockholding limits Sep 1–Nov 30. Sep 3: dealer stock limit HALVED to 200 MT (Sep 15–Nov 20) to release hoarded stock — market read it as less import need and sold off 3.4%. Next catalyst: whether the 1 MMT window is used at all, then extension/enlargement at Oct 31
El Niño peak intensity — NOAA: very strong peak likely Oct–Jan (63% ≥ +2.0°C)

exitTriggers.name: El Niño weakens / fails
exitTriggers.rationale: Was the primary risk — now essentially retired: NOAA's Aug update raised the odds of a very-strong Oct-Dec peak to 95% (from 81% in July), with a 69% chance of exceeding every El Niño on record since 1950. Persistence holds at 97% through early spring 2027. Residual risk is now just a peak that undershoots this already-elevated forecast, not a failure of the event itself.

exitTriggers.name: Hormuz ceasefire IV crush
exitTriggers.rationale: Options re-price down even before underlying moves. Pre-expiry risk. No de-escalation this week — a Kuwaiti-flagged tanker (Al Salam II) was struck transiting the Strait on Aug 26, and Trump's Aug 25 claim that all mines were cleared is disputed by JMIC; the Strait remains effectively closed to normal commercial traffic. Nearby-tenor options IV (Jul/Oct '26, ~23-31%) remains inside the normal band, no crush observed.

exitTriggers.name: Brazilian mill mix stays at sugar
exitTriggers.rationale: Largely retired — mills have pivoted hard to ethanol: 2H-July crush -8.4% YoY, sugar output -17.6% YoY, with the ethanol blend mandate raised to 32%. Residual risk is a mix reversal if ethanol parity flips.

exitTriggers.name: India ethanol policy reversal
exitTriggers.rationale: Govt raises diversion → removes export supply (bullish risk for sugar but kills bear setup).

exitTriggers.name: Theta decay without move
exitTriggers.rationale: ~$3-5/day per OTM call. Manageable but compounds if no move by Q4.

exitTriggers.name: Crowded-long unwind / failed breakout
exitTriggers.rationale: Funds held a record 70,766 net-long in London whites (COT to Aug 25). Two high-volume reversals from 18.66–18.77¢ (Aug 28, Sep 3) make that zone a double top. Lines: 17.65¢ (Sep 3 low) then 17.44¢ (Aug 28 low). A close through both = failed breakout — reassess adds and consider trimming the 19.5¢ leg. A volume close above 18.77¢ retires this trigger.

tailScenario.title: Energy Lockdown → Sugar Deficit

components.mechanism: Brazilian mill mix shift to ethanol

tailScenario.context: 2024/25 deficit was 3.5 MMT → drove sugar +100% to 28¢. Lockdown deficit could be 2-3x larger.
tailScenario.inelasticDemandNote: Sugar is staple food. COVID: consumption fell 3-5%, recovered fast. 1973-74 energy crisis: consumption fell <10%, prices rose 6x.

executedPositions.notes: Selected 18¢ strike vs planned 19¢ — slightly closer to ATM, marginally less asymmetric but higher delta (0.364 vs ~0.30 estimate for 19¢). Feb'27 expiry vs planned Mar'27 — one less month of time value but catches all major catalysts (Indian monsoon Jun-Sep, Brazilian C-S Aug-Oct, El Niño peak Nov-Feb). Net: cleaner risk-reward with marginally tighter convexity.
